full_judgment:
DM Ansar Uddin Ahmed J: This is an application under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure by accused MA Malik for his anticipatory bail in connection with Sylhet Kotwali PS Case No. 4 dated 2.3.93 under section 6 of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance pending in the Court of Thana Magistrate, Sadar, Sylhet 

 2. The case arose out of a petition dated 28.2.93 made by informant Sultana Jasmin Khan (Shaopa), daughter of Abdul Mukit Khan of Sylhet Town to the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet against the petitioner, his brother and mother, all of Moulvi Bazar with their present address in Dhaka city soliciting action under the provisions of Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance on the allegations that her father was an Ex-Chairman of Sylhet Zilla Parishad, a sitting Member of Parliament from a political party and also a politician. She was married with the petitioner on 11.10.91 for a dower of Taka 5,00,000. 00 But it shortly transpired that the petitioner was a greedy man of loose moral character. The other two accused persons instigated him and he accordingly, put pressure upon her to bring dowry of Taka one crore from her father and started threatening her in various ways. On 17.3.92, however, the petitioner went to her paternal house at Sylhet where she was then residing. At about 10-00 O'clock in the night in course of exchange of words on the question of payment of the dowry the petitioner got infuriated and physically assaulted her and attempted to kill her by strangulation. She was somehow saved by others in an unconscious condition. The matter was amicably settled. Again on the night following 18.6.92 while at his own residence at Dhaka the petitioner on hearing a negative reply from her on the question of payment of the dowry dealt a severe blow on her left ear causing profuse bleeding from the ear. Being informed her father took her to Sylhet and arranged her treatment. On the assurance from common relation she again came to the petitioner's house at Dhaka and it was decided that the dispute would be finally settled after his return from London where he was to go in connection with some business. He returned from London on 31.8.92 and in the meantime she had left [or her father's house at Sylhet for her better treatment there. However, the petitioner refused to come to a compromise before payment of the dowry. At last he received from the petitioner's lawyer a notice dated 21.11.92 demanding a huge amount, to which she sent a reply. It may be added, however, that on the very date of submitting the petition to the Deputy Commissioner, that is, on 28.2.93 she instituted Family Suit No.14 of 1993 in the Family Court, Sadar Sylhet for dissolution of the marriage. 

 3. The petition was sent to the police station for necessary action and police on 2.3.93 started Kotwali Police Station Case No. 4 under sections 6 and 9 of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance. Mr. Amirul Kabir Chowdhury, the learned Deputy Attorney-General has informed us that the police has after completion of the investigation submitted charge sheet dated 22.8.94 against the accused petitioner only under section 6 of the said Ordinance. 

 4. On 4.5.94 the petitioner filed an application under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for his anticipatory bail—Criminal Misc. Case No. 525 of 1994—In court No.13. The application appears to have not been pressed and it was accordingly, rejected on 9.5.94 by that Bench (Md. Badruzzaman and M. Fazlul Karim, JJ) under order as follows. "Md. Wahidullah appearing along with Mr. Asrarul Hossain, learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that they have instructions not to press this application. As such the application is rejected as not pressed." 

 5. On 14.8.94 the petitioner filed a similar application before this Bench—Criminal Misc. Case No. 1344 of 1994—without disclosing anything about the earlier application. This application was filed under signature of Mr. Mohammad Shamsul Alam, Advocate. While it was being moved by Mr. Kazi Shahadat Hossain Senior Advocate on 17.8.84, learned Advocate Mr. SK Sinha disclosed about the earlier application, when he was asked to supply the necessary particulars on the following day. On the following day i.e. 18.8.94 Mr. Sinha furnished the particulars, but neither the filing lawyer Mr. Mohammad Shamsul Alam nor his senior Mr. Kazi Shahadat Hossain nor even the accused petitioner was present and the application was rejected by orders as follows. "None appears on call on behalf of the petitioner nor the petitioner himself is present. The application is rejected. 

 12. In reply Mr. Hossain submits that there is no bar to the filing of successive bail applications and that the earlier applications having not been rejected on merit the subsequent application could be pressed on the ground taken in the earlier applications. He also submits that in any view the instant application contains new ground on the question of the jurisdiction of the Court of Sylhet in entertaining the case as the offence, according to the informant's own showing, is alleged to have been committed at Dhaka. In support of his submission the learned Advocate has referred to the decisions reported in 18 DLR 67 and 42 DLR (AD) 223. 

 13. In 18 DLR 67 case it has been held that it is a party's privilege to renew the application for bail until such bail is granted, and in the case reported in 42 DLR (AD) 223 their Lordships have held that it is not correct to say that once a petition for bail is rejected no further application can be made and the remedy lies only in an appeal. We cannot but therefore agree with Mr. Hossain that the instant application is quite maintainable and more particularly so even on no new ground because the earlier applications were rejected otherwise and not on merits. Of course in view of the decision in the case of Zakir Hossain Khan referred to by Mr. Chowdhury we must agree with him that an earlier application for bail having been rejected on merits discarding the ground taken therein similar application subsequently filed without any new ground cannot be considered. We do also add however that subsequent application must contain the information clearly about the earlier application (s) together with prominent heading such as second application or other application and so on and further that such application must be filed before the Bench which had rejected the earlier prayer (s), if of course that Bench is not in the meantime dissolved. 

 14. We have carefully gone through the record and we find that both the parties are men of money and reputation. Further it appears that the informant's father is a very respectable and influential man having easy access to the local executive authorities. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case we are satisfied that there are reasonable grounds for believing that the accused is not guilty of the offence and that his apprehension cannot be ruled out as baseless. Thus not only there is, in our view, good prima facie ground made out for grant of bail in respect of the offence alleged but also we are convinced that if the petitioner were to be arrested and or refused bail such course would in all probability be taken not from motives of furthering the ends of justice but from some other motive with the object of injuring him causing irreparable harm to his reputation and liberty.
